title: Clarkson and colleagues reported northern Australian occupation by 65,000 years ago
summary: The claim is the paper's title. Early dates at this site have been argued over.
body: Chris Clarkson and colleagues, "Human occupation of northern Australia by 65,000 years ago" (Nature, 2017), state the date in the title. Archaeological first-arrival dates are often revised when methods or associations are challenged. This pack did not open a later critique, so the card records the 2017 claim and flags the date as a research result rather than a settled clock. The broader point that stands without the exact millennium is that people reached Sahul by a Pleistocene sea crossing, which is a different history from a story that starts in Europe.
